title.narrative: Malawi Resilience and Disaster Risk Management Project

description.narrative: Support the recovery of livelihoods and infrastructure in flood and drought affected areas and strengthen capacity for flood and drought risk management

The development objective of Drought Recovery and Resilience Project for Malawi is to support the government of Malawi to meet the immediate food security and livelihoods restoration needs of the communities affected by drought and promote recovery and resilience in key affected sectors. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Improving Food Security and Sustainable Livelihoods, aims to improve agricultural productivity, enhance cultivated area under assured irrigation and expand livelihood options for vulnerable populations. It ahs the following subcomponents: (a) Meeting Urgent Food Security Needs; (b) Improving Livelihoods and Building Resilience through Input Distribution; (c) Increasing Agriculture Productivity and Resilience; and (d) Climate Smart Irrigation. 2) The second component, Enhancing Drought-Resilience and Preparedness has the following subcomponents: (a) Rehabilitating and Augmenting Critical Water Supply Infrastructure; (b) Strengthening Water Resource and Catchment Management; (c) Strengthening Drought Resilience (Technical Assistance). 3) The third component, Contingent Emergency Response Component, will allow for rapid reallocation of project proceeds in the event of future natural or man-made disaster or crisis that has caused or is likely to imminently cause a major adverse economic and or social impact during the life of the project. 4) The fourth component, Project Management, will finance the project activities.

condition.narrative: NameProject Steering CommitteeDue Date: 30-Dec-2016Description of the CovenantThe Recipient shall maintain throughout Projectimplementation, a Project Steering Committee with a composition, mandate and other resources satisfactory to the Association. TheProject Steering Committee shall be responsible for providing overall coordination, as well as policy and strategic guidance on theProject, all in accordance with the provisions of the Project Implementation Manual.

Name Maintaining a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) Recurrent Frequency - ContinuousDescription of CovenantThe Recipientshall maintain throughout Project implementation, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) with terms of reference, staffing and otherresources satisfactory to the Association.

Name Project Implementation ManualDue Date: 30-Jan-2017 Description of CovenantThe Recipient shall not later than sixty (60)days after the Effective Date: (i) (A) prepare, under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, and furnish to theAssociation for review, a Project implementation manual containing detailed guidelines and procedures for the implementation of theProject. and (B) thereafter adopt and carry out the Project in accordance with such Project implementation manual as shall havebeen approved by the Association (“Project Implementation Manual”).

Name Project Technical Committee Due Date: 30-Dec-2016 Description of CovenantThe Recipient shall maintain throughout Projectimplementation, a Project Technical Committee with a composition, mandate and other resources satisfactory to the Association. TheProject Technical Committee shall be responsible for, inter alia: (a) providing technical guidance at both strategic andoperational levels and resolving technical issues that are brought to its attention; and (b) ensuring the implementation of theinter-ministerial and inter-departmental coordination modalities, and for managing the respective roles and responsibilities setout for implementing ministries, departments and agencies, all in accordance with the provisions of the Project ImplementationManual.

Name Safeguard InstrumentsDue Date: 30-Dec-2016 Description of CovenantThe Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month afterthe Effective Date: (i) prepare and disclose in a manner satisfactory to the Association: (a) an Environmental and SocialManagementFramework (ESMF), (b) a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), (c) an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP), collectively"Safeguard Instruments" (ii) and ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Safeguard Instruments; and (ii) allmeasures required for carrying out the recommendations of said Safeguard Instruments are taken in a timely manner.

Name Staffing the Project Implementation Unit (PIU)Due Date: 30-Dec-2016 Description of CovenantThe Recipient shall not laterthan thirty (30) days of the Effective Date assign to the PIU, and thereafter maintain through-out Project implementation, anational coordinator, a Project coordinator, an agriculture specialist, an assistant financial management specialist, an assistantmonitoring and evaluation specialist, an assistant safeguards specialist, a Project Accountant, a civil engineer, a monitoring andevaluation and public works coordinator, an administrative assistant, all in accordance with the Procurement Regulations.

The Recipient shall for purposes of implementation of the Project maintain throughout Project implementation, the PMU with termsof reference, staffing and other resources satisfactory to the Association, including the Technical Team and a minimum core set ofstaff consisting of: (i) a Program Coordinator, a Project Management Specialist, a Procurement Specialist, a Financial ManagementSpecialist, an Environmental Safeguards Specialist, a Social Safeguards Specialist, and a Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist; and(ii) an additional Procurement Specialist, Environmental Specialist, Social Specialist, and Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist,all to be hired within two (2) months from the Effective Date

title.narrative: Number of small earth dams rehabilitated

comment.narrative: The Project achieved 78 percent of the end target. The remaining 5 small dams were not constructed due to resource limitations. This indicator was reintroduced into the results framework in the 2023 restructuring, after previously being dropped during the AF. It captures the 12 dams constructed by the parent project and 6 under the AF (even though the AF prepared designs and tender documents for 17).

title.narrative: Hectares of catchments conserved and restored

comment.narrative: The result was 95 percent of the end target, and the indicator was not fully achieved. The original target was reduced in 2023 to reallocate resources towards addressing the impact of Tropical Cyclone Freddy. The full target was not met due to the reduced investment in catchment conservation.

title.narrative: Area provided with new/ rehabilitated irrigation facilities

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's end target. The result reflects people who benefit from investments in climate smart irrigation.

title.narrative: Number of farmers trained in sustainable land and irrigation water management

comment.narrative: The Project trained 4,900 farmers in water management, exceeding the target of 4,870.

title.narrative: Area covered by installed small-scale solar power drip and medium-scale solar pumps

comment.narrative: The project achieved 99% of the end target. This indicator was reintroduced in 2023 from the parent project to capture results not covered under the other indicators. The project developed 14 small-scale solar power drip networks covering 233 hectares and 460 hectares under the medium-scale solar pump scheme.

title.narrative: Number of water supply schemes rehabilitated and upgraded

comment.narrative: The revised end target was achieved. However, this end target had been reduced from 13 in 2023 due to resource limitations. Despite the reduced water supply schemes, the total number of beneficiaries did not reduce due to other investments.

title.narrative: Number of farming households benefitting from restored and enhanced irrigation schemes

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's end target. The result reflects people who benefit from irrigation schemes reconstructed and solar powered drip kit networks established.

title.narrative: Number of farming households benefitting from restored and enhanced irrigation schemes

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's end target. The result reflects people who benefit from irrigation schemes reconstructed and solar powered drip kit networks established.

title.narrative: Number of people with access to improved water supply as a result of the project

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's target. The result reflects people who benefit from the water supply systems rehabilitated/upgraded and boreholes constructed.

title.narrative: Number of people with access to improved water supply as a result of the project

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's target. The result reflects people who benefit from the water supply systems rehabilitated/upgraded and boreholes constructed.

title.narrative: Number of beneficiaries from emergency response and recovery

comment.narrative: The CERC was activated in 2019 following Tropical Cyclone Idai. The beneficiaries are from the related rehabilitation of roads, educational infrastructure, and water and sanitation systems.

title.narrative: Number of hotspot micro catchments with Catchment Management Committees and plans

comment.narrative: The end target was not achieved due to the reallocation of resources away from catchment management and towards the impacts of Tropical Cyclone Freddy.

title.narrative: Number of government departments utilizing project generated data and knowledge products for DRM decision making

comment.narrative: The target for this was significantly overachieved, with twenty government departments utilizing various data and studies generated by the project.

title.narrative: Cumulative crop production from land irrigated under the project

comment.narrative: The project exceeded its end target for crop production under irrigated land.

title.narrative: Number of people in areas with reduced flood risk to project interventions

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's end target. The result reflects people who benefit from investments in protective infrastructure (dykes) and drainage structures.

comment.narrative: The Project exceeded it's end target. The result reflects people who benefit from investments in protective infrastructure (dykes) and drainage structures.

title.narrative: Percentage of grievances registered and addressed within 45 days

comment.narrative: The resolution period for 70 percent of grievances was within 45 days, and the project achieved this target.

title.narrative: Number of operational rural boreholes constructed under the Project

comment.narrative: The project exceeded the end target, which had been revised upwards in 2023 to incorporate an additional 100 boreholes constructed to address the impact of the cholera outbreak.

title.narrative: National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) designed/approved with finalized bidding documents and safeguard instruments

comment.narrative: The NEOC was dropped from the project due to the non-performance of the consultant and subsequent termination of the contract. Given the time and fiscal constraints, it was decided to drop this activity and it will be taken up by the ongoing Regional Climate Resilience Project 2.

title.narrative: National Comprehensive Risk Assessment and risk atlas developed

comment.narrative: A comprehensive multi-hazard risk atlas has been developed, including an online dashboard that is publicly available.
The operation decision support system for Shire River was strengthened by providing real-time data and producing hazard and inundation maps.

title.narrative: Adopted flood risk management plans for Blantyre and Shire River Basin

comment.narrative: The plans developed for flood risk management for Blantyre and the Shire River Basin were adopted.

title.narrative: Number of functional local DRM authorities in Project affected areas established or strengthened

comment.narrative: The Project achieved the end target.

title.narrative: Number of functional local DRM authorities in Project affected areas established or strengthened

comment.narrative: The Project achieved the end target.

title.narrative: Proportion of women in WUA committees (decision-making position)

comment.narrative: The project achieved the end target, with women comprising 40 percent of the Water Users Association (WUA) committees that were established or strengthened under the Project.

title.narrative: Number of DRM plans in affected districts developed and informed by available knowledge and data products

comment.narrative: This indicator was not achieved. Plans were developed for four districts (Blantyre, Tholo, Mwanza, and Neno). However, the remaining were not completed and will be completed under the ongoing Regional Climate Resilience Project 2.

title.narrative: Improved drainage system for flood control - (Length of drainage structures constructed)

comment.narrative: The project exceeded the end target by constructing 7.15 km of drainage structures in Blantyre City.
